indication: ** 18-year-old male presenting with increasing right tibial pain over the last two months. Patient reports prior radiographs performed at primary care physician's office were reportedly negative for anomaly. Evaluate for osteomyelitis versus suspicious bone lesion.
technique: ** Multidetector CT imaging was performed through the right lower extremity from the knee joint to the ankle joint. Axial images were obtained with multiplanar coronal and sagittal reconstructions.
findings:
**
The visualized soft tissues of the right leg are generally unremarkable. There is no evidence of significant subcutaneous edema or large fluid collections within the calf musculature. The neurovascular bundles appear intact without obvious enlargement or abnormal calcifications.
Regarding the osseous structures, there is a highly aggressive appearing lesion centered within the diaphysis of the right tibia. This lesion demonstrates a permeative pattern of bone destruction with ill-defined margins, blending into the surrounding normal medullary bone. Associated with this is an aggressive periosteal reaction, characterized by interrupted cortical continuity and a "sunburst" appearance of new bone formation extending into the adjacent soft tissues. There is mild associated soft tissue swelling surrounding the tibial shaft at the level of the lesion.
The proximal and distal epiphyses of the tibia and fibula are well-maintained. The knee and ankle joints demonstrate preserved joint spaces without significant effusion or erosive changes. The fibula remains intact throughout its length without evidence of cortical breakthrough or suspicious lesions. A small, benign-appearing cortical desmoid is noted at the distal fibular metaphysis, which appears to be a normal developmental variant. The visualized portions of the gastrocnemius and soleus muscles show normal attenuation and morphology.
conclusion:
**
Aggressive permeative lesion involving the diaphysis of the right tibia with associated periosteal reaction, highly suggestive of a primary bone tumor. No evidence of an associated soft tissue abscess.
